When you want to clarify which person or thing you are talking about, you use a relative clause.

You can begin a relative clause with who for people, which for things or that for either people or things.

In spoken English you usually use that, rather than which or who.

You put the relative clause immediately after the noun it talks about.
A subject relative clause describes the subject of the clause.

Example:
The man who called wanted to speak to Tom.
Which man? The man who called.
The clause who called immediately follows man - the noun it describes.
An object relative clause describes the object of the clause.

Example:
Can you return the book that I lent you?
Which book? The book I lent you.

When you are writing a news article or giving an interview, you can include the Simple Past Passive to describe something done by someone at sometime in the past.
In a regular sentence structure, you use subject + verb + object.

Example:
Many concerned locals showed me the negative effects of climate change.
In the Simple Past Passive form, you use the structure:
Object + was / were + past participle + by subject

Example:
I was shown the negative effect of climate change by many concerned locals.
Many books were published by world-renowned authors on the subject.
I think some of those movies were even made by the same director!
Example: Natural disasters have increased globally.

images.text:
Sally: As someone who is constantly studying weather phenomena, what can you tell us about the increase in natural disasters globally?
Brock Tameland: During my recent travels, I was shown the negative effect of climate change by many concerned locals. The fields that they own are getting drier. The freshwater lakes that they use are becoming saturated with pollutants ... This is made even worse by tornadoes and heat waves in the summer, and ice storms and blizzards in the winter.

Sally: Are you saying that the weather is becoming more extreme?
Brock Tameland: Absolutely. The current patterns have become impossible to predict. The data that was collected by our colleagues 20 years ago is now obsolete. The scientists who first studied climate change never imagined that things would get so bad in such a short amount of time.

Sally: This seems to be a problem which people keep ignoring, though.
Brock Tameland: I agree. Many books were published by world-renowned authors on the subject. Even Hollywood is playing its part by releasing blockbusters that are raising awareness on this issue.
Sally: I think some of those movies were even made by the same director! Maybe it's someone who's as concerned about natural disasters as you are!
